claim.summary: For a linear code B in Fq^m with quotient dimension r>=1, let H_B(j) count cosets meeting the support-j ball. If H_B(R)<=q^(eta r), 0<=eta<1, then H_B(K+s)/H_B(K)>=(2-eta)^s for all nonnegative integer K,s with K+s<=R. Ambient Hamming-ball size is a sufficient upper bound for the hypothesis.
claim.assessment: Working application of the published Hamming edge-boundary inequality in Diskin-Samotij equation (3). A basis chosen among coordinate images supplies allowed one-coordinate neighbors in the quotient, and division by maximum boundary incidence yields the growth factor. No evaluation or global multiplication model for the charged quotient is used.

claim.summary: For an arbitrary-field Boolean degree-D pseudoideal J_D and a tuple E_i of degree <=e with e+K<=D, let c(k)=rank(f in V_k -> ([E_i f])_i). If old standard-monomial level j has size <=binomial(X,j) for K-delta<j<=K, X>=K and 1<=delta<=K, then for c(K)>0, c(K-delta)/c(K)>=(1+sum_(i=1)^delta rho^i)^(-1), rho=(X-K+delta)/(K-delta+1). A proved bound on the actual error standard family also suffices.
claim.assessment: Attributed direct extension of the near-half notebook's Kruskal-Katona proof from binary C_D to any Boolean pseudoideal and any coefficient field. Bounded absorption gives a down-closed squarefree standard family; Lovasz shadows give the ratio. The zero-rank case is separate and every weight/prefactor degree is included in e. This does not extend binary rank retention/gain to other fields, and does not assume a source-wide level cap or replace the ratio by the base cumulative Hilbert ratio.

claim.summary: On an n>=4 graph of edge expansion epsilon>0 with nonzero total F3 charge, any refutation of vertex equations by scalar multiplication and binary linear combination has a line with vertex potential support in[n/3,2n/3) and at least epsilon*n/6 nonzero edge coefficients. The final potential is a nonzero constant; the first large support is the union of two smaller ones, and a nonzero level-set cut gives expansion. For fixed-degree constant-expansion families, exact fixed-depth AC0[2] circuits for all such line predicates on the whole valid one-hot cube must include a superpolynomial-size line, by fixing one active edge and reducing to MOD3 on Omega(n) bits. This is a restricted charge-derivation representation lower bound; extraction from arbitrary Frege is unproved.
claim.assessment: Working all-parameter balanced-support proof and circuit restriction, medium reviewed. DAG reuse and cancellations are allowed. No claim that general Frege lines are charge equations, no new circuit lower bound, and no PC-degree conclusion. Compatible with the older balanced character-cut upper proof.
